sections.heading: C — Knowledge dossier: Emergencies, malfunctions and crashes
sections.markdown:
## C — Knowledge dossier: Emergencies, malfunctions and crashes

FACT_ID: sec16-F01 | anchor: A57
The handbook identifies braking, steering and acceleration as options for avoiding a crash or reducing its impact. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F02 | anchor: A57
ABS helps the vehicle stop without skidding while preserving steering control; follow the owner’s instructions for its use. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F03 | anchor: A57
For the handbook’s ABS emergency-braking procedure, press the brake pedal hard and keep pressure applied. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F04 | anchor: A57
An ABS pedal may vibrate or produce clicking during operation, which the handbook describes as normal. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F05 | anchor: A57
Steering remains possible while using ABS, and a vehicle without ABS requires its own manual’s braking procedure. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F06 | anchor: A57
To steer around a hazard, hold the wheel with both hands and aim toward the intended path while avoiding other traffic. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F07 | anchor: A57
After clearing the hazard, countersteer to straighten and regain control before slowing. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F08 | anchor: A57
Acceleration may be needed to avoid a vehicle about to strike from the rear or side. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F09 | anchor: A57
A skid can result from excessive speed for conditions, abrupt stopping or lost tire grip. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F10 | anchor: A57
When a skid begins, release pressure on the brake or accelerator and look toward the desired path. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F11 | anchor: A57
If the wheels leave the pavement, avoid a panic return, slow gradually and steer back only when safe. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec16-F12 | anchor: A58
Follow the vehicle owner’s maintenance schedule to reduce malfunction risk. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F13 | anchor: A58
The handbook warns against driving with a brake warning illuminated and treats it as a reason to investigate brake operation. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F14 | anchor: A58
If brakes fail while moving, the handbook directs gradual parking-brake application to avoid locking the rear wheels and readiness to release it if a skid starts. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F15 | anchor: A58
If the parking-brake response fails, the handbook next says to turn off the engine and find a safe place off the road to stop. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F16 | anchor: A58
Do not continue driving a vehicle whose brakes do not work. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F17 | anchor: A58
A blowout is a rapid loss of tire air; a front blowout pulls sharply toward that side, while a rear blowout may wobble, shake and pull toward it. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F18 | anchor: A58
For a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, maintain a straight path, ease off the accelerator and let speed fall gradually. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F19 | anchor: A58
Avoid braking during a blowout, allowing the vehicle to slow naturally and braking gently only if necessary. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F20 | anchor: A58
After a blowout, leave the road at a safe location if possible, activate emergency flashers and replace the tire. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F21 | anchor: A58
If the engine stops while driving, keep a firm grip because steering may become harder but remains possible. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F22 | anchor: A58
After engine failure, find an escape path, brake steadily instead of hard and pull off the road. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F23 | anchor: A58
Once stopped after engine failure, try restarting; if it fails, raise the hood, use emergency flashers and call for help. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F24 | anchor: A58
The handbook’s stuck-accelerator sequence starts with switching the engine off, selecting Neutral and finding an escape path. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F25 | anchor: A58
Its stuck-accelerator procedure then calls for smooth steering, gentle braking and leaving the roadway, with service-center pedal repair before driving again. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F26 | anchor: A58
For a highway breakdown, make the vehicle visible and notify authorities by phone or another available device. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F27 | anchor: A58
Move a broken-down vehicle away from traffic and activate emergency flashers. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F28 | anchor: A58
The handbook places breakdown-warning flares about 200 to 300 feet behind the disabled vehicle. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec16-F29 | anchor: A58
If headlights fail, try the switch several times; if that fails, use available flashers, turn signals or fog lamps and leave the road promptly. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0058]

Misconceptions: ABS needs sustained pedal pressure; a skid response is a different condition; a moving vehicle’s ignition must not be put into Lock, and this source’s engine-off malfunction instructions need vehicle-specific confirmation.
Mnemonics: Use condition, control, safe stopping and help as an authored emergency cue.
Glossary: ABS means anti-lock braking system; a blowout is rapid tire deflation; an uneven drop-off is departure from the paved surface; a secondary collision is another impact after the initial crash.
Dynamic facts: Controls differ by vehicle and roadside conditions change; the owner’s manual supplies applicable operating details. Published violation rankings are undated.

ranked.label: Pedagogic emphasis: Choose the response for the actual emergency and preserve crash-scene duties.

items.why: Braking, skids, mechanical failures, crash response and reporting require distinct scenarios.

corpus_stability.reason: The official dated snapshot is pinned, but revision frequency has not been measured. Unknown cadence remains blocked for release pending the section-A verification debt; this is not a claim that the handbook is volatile.
